# Metrics glossary

What every number in the backtest and portfolio tables means.

- **Annual return** — Average daily return scaled to a year. On its own it says little; always look at the risk taken to earn it.
- **Annual volatility** — How much returns fluctuate. 20% volatility roughly means returns stay within ±20% of the average in about two years out of three.
- **Sharpe ratio** — Return per unit of volatility. Roughly: below 0.5 weak, 0.5–1 reasonable, above 1 good, above 2 exceptional (and worth questioning). The main yardstick for comparing models.
- **Sortino ratio** — Like Sharpe but counting only downside volatility as risk. If it is clearly higher than Sharpe, rallies are sharper than sell-offs.
- **Max drawdown** — The deepest loss after a peak. Recovering from a 30% drawdown takes a 43% gain. Compare it with what you could stomach.
- **CVaR 95%** — Average daily loss on the worst 5% of days. 3% means the portfolio loses about 3% on a typical bad day.
- **Effective number of assets** — 1 / Σw². How many assets the weights are really spread across: with 6 assets, 6 is perfectly balanced and 1.5 means nearly all in one.
- **Risk contribution** — How much of total risk comes from one asset. An asset with 20% of capital but 40% of risk is the portfolio's main risk driver.
- **Walk-forward backtest** — The model is trained on one window of history, tested on the next (unseen) period, and the window rolls forward. The closest test to real use, though it excludes fees and taxes.
- **Time-weighted return (TWR)** — Strips out the effect of deposits and withdrawals, measuring only investment skill. Used to compare against funds and benchmarks.
- **XIRR (money-weighted return)** — Annual return that accounts for when your money went in and out. It is the return you actually experienced; the gap to TWR is the effect of your timing.
- **Real return** — Inflation-adjusted return: (1 + return) / (1 + inflation) − 1. Shows whether your purchasing power actually grew.
